summary: When a charged crystal ball is used to find furniture such as the up stairs, C reveals the location and enters browse_map(); that calls getpos(), whose first invocation displays the farlook tip. JavaScript reaches detect.js:furniture_detect() but substitutes note_unported('detect.c browse_map') for this call, leaving the base map on screen. The v46 replay first differs at step 39 when C shows the tip header and JavaScript shows no header.

source.branch: furniture_detect() (1091-1134) scans visible map cells, applies magic_map_background() to furniture and reveals furniture mimics. If any glyph changes, it calls browse_map(TER_DETECT | TER_MAP | TER_TRP | TER_OBJ | TER_MON, "location"); browse_map() enters getpos(), which calls handle_tip(TIP_GETPOS) on its first use. The no-new-glyph arm instead calls display_nhwindow(WIN_MAP, TRUE).
callers: apply.c:doapply (4358-4360) calls detect.c:use_crystal_ball() for CRYSTAL_BALL; use_crystal_ball() (1334-1343) calls furniture_detect() when the requested character is a furniture symbol. JavaScript follows apply.js:doapply -> detect.js:use_crystal_ball -> furniture_detect.
artifact.c:arti_invoke (2140-2145) is a second production caller of use_crystal_ball() for crystal-ball artifacts; JavaScript artifacts.js:arti_invoke routes to detect.js:use_crystal_ball.

detect.c:browse_map() (104-117) calls getpos() with autodescribe and the detection terrain mask. getpos.c:getpos() (838-839) calls handle_tip(TIP_GETPOS); JavaScript counterparts already exist in detect.js:browse_map, getpos.js:getpos, and hack.js:handle_tip.
dependencies: detect.c:browse_map() and detect.c:map_redisplay() already have JavaScript implementations in detect.js. The missing production wiring is in furniture_detect().

furniture_detect() also calls unconstrain_map(), glyph_at(), glyph_to_cmap(), magic_map_background(), m_at(), seemimic(), canspotmon(), map_invisible(), and map_redisplay(); their JavaScript implementations are already present.

The alternate no-new-glyph arm calls display_nhwindow(WIN_MAP, TRUE), currently represented by note_unported('detect.c display_nhwindow') in JavaScript. Keep that named gap unless its TTY callee is separately owned and source-traced; the selected route uses the revealed-glyph browse_map arm.

selectionReason: The saved v46 mismatch at the crystal-ball furniture screen reaches detect.c:furniture_detect. The first C-only output is caused by its revealed-glyph branch calling browse_map, which then invokes getpos and the first-use TIP_GETPOS callback. The same-file browse_map and map_redisplay helpers already exist in JavaScript; the missing call is the actionable owner.
evidence: Queue SHA-256 e381a612fbd22667de87ac4a6627c90a0f4164c63559cd4be9d84ee756b8a3b2 identifies v46-crystal-ball-furniture-attempt10: 40/42 screens, 2544/2544 RNG calls, and 41/42 cursors matched. Its first mismatch is segment 0, step 39, screen row 0 column 10 (C: T, JavaScript: space), cursor C [16,8,1] versus JavaScript [39,5,1].

Upstream detect.c:1091-1134 shows furniture_detect() calling browse_map() when the scan reveals glyphs and calling map_redisplay() after either branch. detect.c:1334-1343 shows use_crystal_ball() dispatching furniture symbols to furniture_detect(). drawing.c:def_char_is_furniture() (120-140) puts the up-stair symbol in this category.

The production entry trace is apply.c:4358-4360 -> detect.c:use_crystal_ball:1334-1343 -> furniture_detect:1127-1132 -> browse_map:104-117 -> getpos.c:getpos:838-839 -> hack.c:handle_tip:1852-1880 -> nhcore.lua:108-123 show_getpos_tip(). artifact.c:2142-2143 is the alternate use_crystal_ball caller.

At the examined commit, detect.js:1327-1330 records note_unported('detect.c browse_map') rather than invoking its existing browse_map() at 429-448. Thus JavaScript skips the getpos/first-use tip window; the selected recording shows C’s farlook tip header at step 39 while JavaScript remains on the base map.
